THIS GRANT WILL ALLOW ADELANTE CENTERS GARFIELD PRODUCE TO MAKE THE KEY INVESTMENTS THAT WILL FACILITATE IMPLEMENTATION OF A CONSUMER FACING RETAIL ORGANIC MICROGREEN PRODUCT, INCLUDING BRAND DEVELOPMENT, MARKETING, AND PRODUCT PROMOTION IN NEW AND EXISTING DISTRIBUTION CHANNELS. WE WILL ALSO UPGRADE FARM EQUIPMENT TO FACILITATE ORGANIC PACKAGING, HANDLING, FOOD SAFETY, ENVIRONMENTAL CONTROLS, AND FARM AUTOMATION.  ADELANTE WILL FACILITATE A ONE DAY CONFERENCE TO NETWORK EXISTING RURAL AND URBAN ORGANIC PRODUCERS TO SHARE BEST AGRICULTURAL PRACTICES AND ESTABLISH AND TEST AN ALTERNATIVE REFRIGERATED PRODUCE PICK UP AND DELIVERY COLLECTIVE SYSTEM (ALTERNATIVE SUPPLY CHAIN) WITH THE PURPOSE OF REDUCING LOGISTICS COSTS TO ACCESS THE CHICAGO MARKET. THIS WILL ALLOW BOTH GARFIELD PRODUCE PRODUCTS AND A MORE EXTENSIVE LIST OF SMALLER LOCAL ORGANIC PRODUCERS TO BUILD COLLECTIVE CAPACITY TO GROW INTO LARGER, MORE PROFITABLE, URBAN CONSUMER MARKETS.   FINALLY, WE WILL CONDUCT A FEASIBILITY STUDY TO ASSESS THE COST AND BENEFIT OF EXPANSION INTO NEW MARKETS FOR ORGANIC PRODUCTS IN MILWAUKEE, ST. LOUIS AND INDIANAPOLIS.  THESE PROGRAMS WILL INCREASE LOCAL URBAN AGRICULTURE JOBS, EXPAND BUSINESS CAPACITY AND ALLOW ORGANIC PRODUCTS TO REACH LOCAL CONSUMERS THAT WOULD OTHERWISE NEVER HAVE ACCESS TO NOR UNDERSTAND THE BENEFIT OF ORGANIC PRODUCE.

AMALTHEIA ORGANIC DAIRY, LLC IS SEEKING FUNDING TO PROVIDE WHOLESOME ORGANIC PASTEURIZED GOAT MILK TO THE PUBLIC IN OUR HEALTH-CONSCIOUS COMMUNITY. MEL AND SUE BROWN SET ABOUT THEIR GRADE A AMALTHEIA DAIRY OPERATION ON THANKSGIVING DAY 2000. THEY STARTED MILKING WITH 90 GOATS AND HAVE NOW GROWN THE OPERATION TO 265 GOATS. WHILE THEY CURRENTLY ONLY SELL CHEESES, THEY ARE ASKED MULTIPLE TIMES A WEEK IF THEY HAVE GOAT MILK AVAILABLE FOR SALE AND WOULD LIKE TO EXPAND THEIR OFFERINGS BY SELLING PASTEURIZED GOAT MILK TO CONSUMERS AND GROCERY STORES. WE PLAN TO SPEND OMDG FUNDING ON EQUIPMENT AND INSTALLATION COSTS FOR A GLYCOL CHILLER, A BOTTLER, A PLATE CHILLER, AND BOTTLES. THIS WILL ALLOW US TO SELL 2,500 GALLONS DURING OUR FIRST YEAR AND INCREASE THAT AMOUNT OVER COMING YEARS TO MEET DEMAND. THIS WILL INCREASE OUR ANNUAL INCOME BY A MINIMUM OF 32,500. AMALTHEIA HAS PREVIOUSLY WORKED WITH LOCAL AND NATIONAL GROCERY STORE CHAINS AND DISTRIBUTORS IN DENVER AND SEATTLE. WE ALREADY HAVE INTEREST IN SELLING OUR MILK FROM MULTIPLE GROCERY STORES. OFFERING ORGANIC MILK WILL HELP ADDRESS BOTH A LOCAL AND REGIONAL NEED IN THE ORGANIC MARKET.THE OBJECTIVES OF OUR PROJECT INCLUDE: 1) PURCHASE THE NECESSARY EQUIPMENT 2) INSTALL MILKING EQUIPMENT AND 3) SELL GOAT MILK. THE GOALS OF OUR PROJECT INCLUDE: 1) EXPAND LOCAL ACCESS TO ORGANIC GOAT MILK 2) EXPAND REGIONAL ACCESS TO ORGANIC GOAT MILK AND 3) INCREASE RESILIENCY OF AMALTHEIA ORGANIC DAIRY. THE PRIMARY BENEFICIARY OF THIS EQUIPMENT PURCHASE WILL BE AMALTHEIA ORGANIC DAIRY. HOWEVER, OUR OFFERING WILL AFFECT MANY LOCAL AND REGIONAL CONSUMERS THAT DO NOT CURRENTLY HAVE ACCESS TO ORGANIC GOAT MILK. WE PLAN TO START SELL OUR MILK TO GROCERY STORES AND WILL EXPLORE EXPANDING OUR MARKET REACH OUTSIDE OF THIS OVER THE COMING YEARS. WE ANTICIPATE SELLING MILK TO AT LEAST 3 GROCERY STORES IN OUR AREA WITHIN THE FIRST YEAR OF EQUIPMENT INSTALLATION. OUR MILK WILL HELP SUPPORT THEIR SALES. WE WILL NOT HAVE ANY SUBRECIPIENTS, COLLABORATORS, AND PARTNERS FOR THIS GRANT OUTSIDE OF AMALTHEIA ORGANIC DAIRY. HOWEVER, AS OUTLINED ABOVE, THERE WILL BE MULTIPLE BENEFICIARIES AS A RESULT OF THIS FUNDING OUTSIDE OF THE APPLICANT. THIS EQUIPMENT PURCHASE WILL HELP ADDRESS A CURRENT HOLE IN THE MARKET FOR ORGANIC GOAT MILK.

BERRYBROOK ORGANICS LLC (BERRYBROOK) IS A CERTIFIED ORGANIC FARM AND VALUE-ADDED PROCESSING COMPANY NEAR MARION, SD. THIS GROWTH WILL MAKE SIOUX FALLS ONE OF THE FASTEST-GROWING CITIES IN THE UNITED STATES. ACCORDING TO A 2022 REPORT BY THE ORGANIC TRADE ASSOCIATION, ORGANIC FOOD SALES IN THE UNITED STATES REACHED 63.1 BILLION IN 2021, AN INCREASE OF 13.5 FROM THE PREVIOUS YEAR. ORGANIC EGGS WERE ONE OF THE FASTEST-GROWING CATEGORIES, WITH SALES INCREASING BY 17.3 IN 2021.THE EQUIPMENT REQUESTED ADDRESSES TWO NEEDS SUPPLY CHAIN MANAGEMENT IMPROVEMENT THROUGH THE PURCHASE OF A DELIVERY VEHICLE AND PROCESSING EFFICIENCY THROUGH THE PURCHASE OF AN EGG GRADER MACHINE FOR ORGANIC EGG PROCESSING.IN ADDRESSING THESE TWO AREAS OF NEED, BERRYBROOK S GOALS ARE TO SOLIDIFY THE EFFICACY OF THE SUPPLY CHAIN IN PROVIDING SAFE AND RELIABLE GOODS TO MARKETS, INCREASE ACCESS TO MARKETS FOR BERRYBROOK S ORGANIC PRODUCTS, AND INCREASE ORGANIC EGG PROCESSING EFFICIENCY.BERRYBROOK IS AT 100 CAPACITY WITH THEIR CURRENT DELIVERY LOGISTICS. BY OPENING ADDITIONAL DELIVERY CAPACITY, IT REMOVES THE CURRENT LIMIT ON POTENTIAL SALES PER TRIP. DESPITE REGULAR INQUIRIES FROM POTENTIAL CUSTOMERS, BERRYBROOK HAS NOT ACCEPTED ANY NEW ACCOUNTS SINCE 2018. WITH A TRANSPORT VEHICLE, BERRYBROOK WOULD BE ABLE TO SUPPLY MORE ORGANIC PRODUCTS TO REGIONAL MARKETS.BERRYBROOK CURRENTLY USES A PERSONAL VEHICLE FOR TRANSPORT CAPABLE OF HAULING 400 DOZEN EGGS OR AROUND 700 LBS. THE PROPOSED DELIVERY VEHICLES MAXIMUM CAPACITY IS 3800 LBS, A 440 INCREASE. BY INCREASING CAPACITY AND ALLEVIATING THE USE OF A PERSONAL VEHICLE FOR PRODUCT TRANSPORT, THIS EQUIPMENT WOULD HAVE A MAJOR IMPACT ON TRAVEL EMISSIONS, AVAILABILITY OF TRANSPORT, AND MILE RADIUS THAT BERRYBROOK CAN BRING THEIR ORGANIC GOODS TO MARKET.THE REQUESTED EGG GRADER WILL RESULT IN AN INCREASE OF 25 IN PROCESSING EFFICIENCY DUE TO TIME SAVED. CURRENTLY, EGGS ARE NOT INDIVIDUALLY GRADED, DUE TO THE TIME AND LABOR REQUIRED TO MANUALLY WEIGH EACH EGG. THE PROPOSED EGG GRADER WOULD ELIMINATE THE NEED FOR MANUAL GRADING, ALLOWING EGGS TO BE GRADED QUICKLY AND ACCURATELY.THE FARMS CURRENT ORGANIC CERTIFICATION WOULD ALLOW NEARLY DOUBLE THE CURRENT LAYING HEN FLOCK WITHIN THE EXISTING FARM FACILITIES. SO, THE INCREASED PROCESSING EFFICIENCY WOULD ALLOW BERRYBROOK THE OPTION TO THEREBY INCREASE THEIR SALES, AND THE VOLUME OF ORGANIC PRODUCTS THEY CAN BRING TO MARKET.THE SOLE BENEFICIARY OF THE EQUIPMENT IS BERRYBROOK ORGANICS. THE EQUIPMENT STRENGTHENS BERRYBROOKS CAPACITY BY SOLIDIFYING THE EFFICACY OF THE SUPPLY CHAIN IN TRANSPORTING GOODS TO MARKET. THIS WOULD OPEN NEW MARKETS FOR THEIR ORGANIC GOODS, ENSURE SAFETY AND QUALITY OF THE PRODUCT, AND OPEN AN AVENUE FOR GROWTH OF THE OPERATION. THIS EQUIPMENT WOULD BE TRANSFORMATIVE IN HOW BERRYBROOK CRAFTS THEIR ENTIRE OPERATIONAL CAPACITY AND STRATEGY.

match_name: Bickford Farms Inc. dba Meadowlark Organics
prime_award_base_transaction_description: THE PROJECTS PURPOSE IS TO EXPAND PROCESSING CAPACITY AND ESTABLISH MARKET PATHWAYS FOR DOMESTIC ORGANIC GRAIN GROWERS IN THE UPPER MIDWEST. BICKFORD FARMS INC. DBA MEADOWLARK ORGANICS, HAS BECOME AN INTEGRAL PART OF THE REGIONAL GRAIN ECONOMY IN THE DRIFTLESS REGION OF WISCONSIN AND MINNESOTA. SINCE 2015 OWNERS JOHN AND HALEE WEPKING HAVE SUCCESSFULLY CULTIVATED CERTIFIED ORGANIC, FOOD-GRADE GRAINS, AND ESTABLISHED A WHOLESALE AND DIRECT MARKETED FLOUR AND GRAIN BUSINESS. WHEN JOHN AND HALEE BEGAN FARMING AT BICKFORD FARMS INC. THEY SAW AN OPPORTUNITY TO GROW ORGANIC CULINARY GRAINS ON A SCALE THAT COULD SUPPLY AN EXISTING LOCAL STONE MILL. HOWEVER, THE INFRASTRUCTURE OF GRAIN STORAGE AND CLEANING IN THE REGION WAS CRITICALLY LACKING. IN 2017, BICKFORD FARMS INC. WAS AWARDED A USDA VALUE ADDED PRODUCERS GRANT, WHICH BUILT OUT THEIR BRAND MEADOWLARK ORGANICS (MLO), AND INITIATED THEIR WHOLESALE AND DIRECT TO CONSUMER BUSINESSES. IN 2020, MLO PURCHASED MILLING EQUIPMENT FROM LONESOME STONE MILLING IN LONE ROCK, WI AND LAUNCHED THEIR ON-FARM FLOUR MILL, MEADOWLARK COMMUNITY MILL (MCM). THIS VERTICAL INTEGRATION ENABLES GROWING, STORAGE, CLEANING, MILLING, PACKAGING, AND DISTRIBUTION FROM A SINGLE LOCATION. MLOS MISSION IS TO CUSTOM CLEAN AND STORE GRAIN FOR NEIGHBORING FARMERS WHO ARE CONSERVATION-MINDED ORGANIC GROWERS. WITH OMDG FUNDING, MLO WILL UPGRADE THE ON-FARM GRANARY, INCORPORATING NECESSARY EQUIPMENT FOR CUSTOM CLEANING AND EASE OF HANDLING. THE FOLLOWING EQUIPMENT WILL BE PURCHASED FROM COMMODITY TRADERS INTERNATIONAL AND BE INSTALLED IN OUR GRANARY: 1) A USED OLIVER 160 GRAVITY TABLE WHICH SEPARATES GRAIN BASED ON DENSITY, IMPROVING THE TEST-WEIGHT AND PURITY OF CROPS TO MEET THE SPECIFICATIONS NEEDED TO SELL TO GRAIN BUYERS AND PROCESSORS AND 2) A NEW UNIVERSAL MODEL C3 BUCKET ELEVATOR TO GENTLY MOVE GRAIN BETWEEN PIECES OF EQUIPMENT AND 3) A NEW PIKASEN FMS 2000 OPTICAL SORTER WHICH WILL INCREASE THE PURITY OF PRODUCTS SUCH AS DRY EDIBLE BEANS, POPCORN, AND OATS, REMOVING OFF-COLORED AND UNDESIRABLE PARTICLES. THIS IS A CRITICAL STEP IN SORTING LOTS WHICH CONTAIN MULTIPLE CROPS, SUCH AS POPCORN AND DRY BEANS THAT WERE POLY-CROPPED AND HARVESTED AT THE SAME TIME. THIS IS A PRACTICE WE HAVE SUCCESSFULLY EXECUTED ON OUR FARM, AND CURRENTLY RELY ON OUR FANNING MILL TO SEPARATE THE POPCORN AND BEANS BASED ON SIZE. HOWEVER, THE OPTICAL SORTER WILL ALLOW US TO SORT MORE PRECISELY, AND GROW AND CLEAN A WIDER VARIETY OF CULTIVARS, WHICH ARE PREFERRED IN THE FOOD-GRADE MARKETPLACE. WITH OMDG FUNDING, MLO WILL ENHANCE THEIR GRAIN CLEANING INFRASTRUCTURE TO FACILITATE MARKET PATHWAYS FOR ORGANIC ALTERNATIVE CULINARY GRAIN CROPS, SUCH AS WHEAT, CORN, OATS, RYE, SPELT, BUCKWHEAT AND DRY BEANS. OFTEN, THESE CROPS ARE NOT VALUED IN THE COMMODITY CROP MARKET, MAKING IT DIFFICULT FOR FARMERS TO FIND MARKETS FOR THESE VARIETIES. MLO WILL ACT AS A BRIDGE BETWEEN FARMERS GROWING SPECIALTY VARIETIES AND THE MARKET THROUGH TARGETED STORYTELLING, HIGHLIGHTING THE SOIL HEALTH BENEFITS OF INCLUDING ALTERNATIVE GRAIN CROPS IN ROTATION. FARMERS, WHOLESALERS AND CONSUMERS ALL BENEFIT FROM THIS EXPANDED ACCESS, STRENGTHENING THE REGIONS AGRICULTURAL AND ECONOMIC WELL-BEING, AS MORE DIVERSE CROP ROTATIONS ARE EMPLOYED AND CHANNELED TO MARKET.KEY PARTNERS INCLUDE DRIFTLESS REGION FARMERS: KEITH SPELTZ FARM, KOETHER FAMILY FARM, WILSON ORGANIC FARM, DOLAN FAMILY FARM, OTTER CREEK FARM, SEVEN SEEDS FARM, AND OTHERS IN SOUTHERN WISCONSIN AND EASTERN MINNESOTA. WITH INCREASED CAPACITY, THE INTENTION IS TO SERVE AN ADDITIONAL 10 ORGANIC FARMS WITHIN OUR REGION. MCM, THE MAIN PURCHASER OF FOOD GRADE GRAINS FROM MLO, WILL BENEFIT SUBSTANTIALLY, MILLING THE INCREASED GRAIN FLOW, AND CHANNELING IT INTO THE FOODSHED THROUGH BAKERIES, GROCERY STORES, RESTAURANTS AND RETAIL LOCATIONS. CREAM OF THE WEST WILL BOLSTER CURRENT EDUCATIONAL ENDEAVORS TO EXPAND, EXPONENTIALLY INCREASING AUDIENCE THROUGH BOTH BOOTS ON THE GROUND AT SITE EVENTS AS WELL AS RAMPED UP SOCIAL MEDIA ENDEAVORS, PODCASTS, AND VIDEO SERIES. THE INTENDED BENEFICIARIES ARE LOCAL MONTANA FARMERS-PROCESSORS-PARTNERS IN THE INDUSTRY, LOCAL SCHOOL CHILDREN, PLANT STAFF, THE COMMUNITY OF HARLOWTON, MONTANA, AND ANYONE WHO EATS.

THIS PROJECT WILL INCREASE ACCESS FOR LOCAL ORGANIC PRODUCTS TO LARGE SCALE NORTHEAST GROCERY CHAINS BY PROVIDING INDUSTRY STANDARD, COST EFFECTIVE CUSTOM PACKAGING OF PRODUCE FOR SMALL ORGANIC FARMS. ORGANIC PRODUCTS IN THE NORTHEAST MID-ATLANTIC REGION ARE SIGNIFICANTLY UNDERREPRESENTED IN LARGE SCALE GROCERY MARKETS WHERE THE VAST MAJORITY OF ORGANIC FOOD PRODUCTS ARE SOLD. SMALL ORGANIC FARMS IN OUR REGION DO NOT HAVE ACCESS TO AUTOMATED PACKAGING MACHINERY THAT CAN PORTION AND PACK BULK PRODUCE INTO RETAIL SIZE, INDUSTRY STANDARD UPC LABELLED UNITS FOR LARGE SCALE RETAIL SALE. CURRENTLY, SMALL ORGANIC FARMS ARE PACKAGING BY HAND INTO EXPENSIVE SMALL RUN PACKAGES. REDUCING PACKAGING COSTS WILL ALLOW THESE FARMS TO INCREASE PRODUCTION VOLUME AND SALES REVENUE TO LARGE SCALE GROCERY WHERE MOST ORGANIC FOOD IS PURCHASED BUT LOCAL PRODUCE IS UNDERREPRESENTED BECAUSE OF PROFIT MARGIN HURDLES. OVER THE 24 MONTH TERM OF THE PROJECT MACHINERY WILL BE PURCHASED, INSTALLED AND CALIBRATED TO PROVIDE CUSTOM PACKAGING FOR FOUR FARMS WITH THE FOLLOWING GOALS:1) INCREASE THE MARKET SHARE OF ORGANIC PRODUCTS IN LARGE SCALE GROCERY STORES THROUGHOUT THE NORTHEAST.2) DECREASE UNIT COST OF SMALL ORGANIC FARM PRODUCT PACKAGING FOR RETAIL GROCERY SALES MAKING THESE PRODUCTS MORE COMPETITIVE WHILE INCREASING SALES VOLUME.3) INCREASE LABOR EFFICIENCY BY REDUCING OR ELIMINATING LOW SKILL PACKAGING TASKS AND PROVING HIGHER SKILL AND ULTIMATELY HIGHER VALUE TASKS FOR WORKERS ON ORGANIC FARMS.4)FOSTER AND STRENGTHEN CONNECTIONS BETWEEN SMALL ORGANIC FARMS TO DEVELOP SHARED PATHWAYS TOWARDS EXPANDED MARKETS.

NORTHERN MICHIGAN IS HOME TO MANY ORGANIC PRODUCERS, YET NO CAPABILITY EXISTS FOR ORGANIC PRODUCERS TO DEVELOP ORGANIC PACKAGED PRODUCTS WITH THE RAW ORGANIC COMMODITIES THEY PRODUCE. THE PURPOSE OF THIS PROJECT IS TO EXPAND MARKET ACCESS FOR NEW ORGANIC PACKAGED PRODUCTS BY ESTABLISHING AGGREGATION AND CO-MANUFACTURING SERVICES SERVING MULTIPLE ORGANIC PRODUCERS IN NORTHERN MICHIGAN INITIALLY, WITH CONTINUED GROWTH THROUGHOUT THE MIDWEST. AS A USDA ORGANIC CERTIFIED ORGANIC HANDLER AND PROCESSING FACILITY, CULTURED FERMENTS IS WELL-POSITIONED TO INTRODUCE THESE SERVICES AND TRANSFORM FROM A SINGULAR PRODUCT LINE FACILITY TO THE ABILITY TO PACKAGE ALMOST ANY VISCOUS PRODUCT IN AN ORGANIC FORMAT. FURTHERMORE, THIS PROJECT WILL ENABLE PRODUCT DEVELOPMENT OF ORGANIC KOMBUCHA MADE AVAILABLE IN CANS ALONG WITH EXISTING GLASS BOTTLE FORMATS. THIS PROJECT INCLUDES THE FOLLOWING ACTIVITIES: INSTALLATION OF A CANNING LINE TO PRODUCE ORGANIC KOMBUCHA IN CANNED FORMAT, PARTNER WITH AREA ORGANIC PRODUCERS TO PROVIDE CO-MANUFACTURING SERVICES, EXPAND DELIVERY NETWORKS AND MAXIMIZE EFFICIENCY, AND SERVE AREA ORGANIC PRODUCERS INCLUDING SMALL AND UNDERSERVED ORGANIC PRODUCERS WITH ACCESS TO NEW MARKETS.THE EXPECTED OUTCOMES WILL BE EXPANDED NETWORKS FOR ORGANIC PRODUCERS PARTICULARLY THOSE IN HISTORICALLY UNDERSERVED AREAS TO DEVELOP AND DELIVER ORGANIC PACKAGED PRODUCTS AND ACCESS NEW MARKETS. BENEFICIARIES INCLUDE NEW CLIENTS THAT CAN ACCESS CO-MANUFACTURING AND DISTRIBUTION SERVICES FOR PACKAGED ORGANIC PRODUCTS, NEW CLIENTS WHO BENEFIT FROM THE OPPORTUNITY TO ADD CANNED BEVERAGES TO THEIR PORTFOLIO, RETAIL CUSTOMERS (CONSUMERS) AND COMMUNITY PARTNERS WHO RECEIVE NEW ACCESS TO ORGANIC PRODUCTS IN NEW, UNDERSERVED MARKETS WHERE DISTRIBUTION IS CURRENTLY LIMITED. THE LARGER COMMUNITY ALSO BENEFITS FROM CREATION OF JOBS AND CREATION OF NEW BUSINESS IN A SMALL, SOCIOECONOMICALLY DISADVANTAGED RURAL COMMUNITY. LOCAL ORGANIC FARMERS WILL ALSO BENEFIT FROM PRIVATE DISTRIBUTION, WHICH IS LESS COSTLY.SEVERAL ORGANIC OPERATORS (FARMS AND OTHER FOOD COMPANIES) HAVE EXPRESSED SUPPORT FOR OUR PROJECT BECAUSE OF THE ACCESS TO NEW MARKETS AND PRODUCT DEVELOPMENT ACTIVITIES IT WILL ENABLE. ENGAGED PARTNERS THROUGHOUT THE REGION WILL STRENGTHEN THE ORGANIC FOOD SYSTEM IN NORTHERN MICHIGAN AND SUPPORT THE VALUE OF USDA ORGANIC.

THE ORGANIC GRAIN GATEWAY OF IOWA (OGGI) PROJECT, IF APPROVED UNDER THIS GRANT PROGRAM, WILL HELP STABILIZE THE ORGANIC GRAINS AND LIVESTOCK FEED SUPPLY CHAIN.  IT WILL OFFER NEW MARKET ACCESS FOR IOWAS ORGANIC GRAIN FARMERS, REDUCE RELIANCE ON FOREIGN IMPORTS FOR THE COASTAL ORGANIC LIVESTOCK MARKETS AND ULTIMATELY INCREASE ORGANIC GRAIN PRODUCTION IN IOWA. THIS WILL BE ACHIEVED BY ASSEMBLING A DEDICATED ORGANIC GRAIN AGGREGATION AND MARKETING TERMINAL IN CENTRAL IOWA WITH EXISTING DIRECT ACCESS TO NORFOLK SOUTHERN, BNSF AND UNION PACIFIC RAILROADS  THE ONLY SITE IN IOWA WITH THIS CONNECTIVITY.BY THE END OF THE PROJECT, IOWAS ORGANIC CORN AND SOYBEAN FARMERS WILL SEE INCREASED DEMAND OF ORGANIC PRODUCTS, SPECIFICALLY ON THE EAST AND WEST COASTS WHICH CURRENTLY RELY ON FOREIGN IMPORTS TO MEET REGIONAL DEMAND FOR THESE PRODUCTS. BY CONNECTING THESE THREE CRITICAL RAILWAYS IN ONE LOCATION, CENTRALLY LOCATED IN THE LARGEST PRODUCING STATE OF ORGANIC CORN AND SOYBEANS, ORGANIC FARMERS IN THE STATE OF IOWA WILL HAVE DIRECT ACCESS TO NEW MARKETS.APPLICANT DES MOINES INDUSTRIAL (DSMI) AND PARTNER ORGANIZATION SUNRISE FOODS HAVE BEEN WORKING TOGETHER SINCE 2022 ON PLANNING, ENGINEERING AND MARKET SUPPORT.  SUNRISE FOODS IS THE LARGEST ORGANIC GRAIN COMPANY IN THE WORLD PURCHASING OVER 11,000,000 BUSHELS OF ORGANIC CORN PER YEAR (MORE THAN WHAT THE STATE OF IOWA GROWS TODAY).  DSMI OWNS A ONE-OF-A-KIND FACILITY IN CENTRAL IOWA WITH EXISTING TRACK AND INFRASTRUCTURE TO SUPPORT THE MODIFICATIONS PROPOSED IN THIS PROJECT SCOPE CAPABLE OF AGGREGATING AND COMPETITIVELY DISTRIBUTING THE VOLUMES REQUIRED BY THE COASTAL DAIRY AND POULTRY INDUSTRIES.  TOGETHER, WITH THE SUPPORT OF IOWA ORGANIC FARMERS, USDA NOP TOPP PARTNERS, IOWA DEPARTMENT OF AGRICULTURE AND THE ORGANIC TRADE ASSOCIATION, THE PROJECT WILL BE A CRUCIAL STEP IN SUSTAINING THE GROWTH IN DOMESTIC ORGANIC PRODUCTION BY PROVIDING THE INFRASTRUCTURE AND MARKET ACCESS NEEDED.

THE PURPOSE OF THIS PROJECT IS TO CREATE A MARKETPLACE TO SELL ORGANIC FEEDS. IN OUR AREA, THERE CURRENTLY EXISTS A GAP IN THE SUPPLY CHAIN BETWEEN ORGANIC COMMODITIES THAT ARE BEING GROWN IN THE AREA AND THE ORGANIC FEED BEING CONSUMED IN THE AREA. GROWING A HEALTHY ORGANIC CROP IS ONLY THE BEGINNING STEP IN CREATING A NUTRITIOUS FEED FOR ORGANIC ANIMALS. SPECIALIZED MACHINES AND EQUIPMENT ARE USED TO TURN VARIOUS ORGANIC COMMODITIES INTO PRECISE RATIONS AND MIXTURES FOR FEEDS. FARMERS GROW ORGANIC CROPS INTENDED FOR ANIMAL FEED, BUT ARE UNABLE TO SELL LOCALLY BECAUSE THE ABILITY AND OR CAPACITY TO PROCESS THE ORGANIC COMMODITY INTO ANIMAL FEED IS UNAVAILABLE. THUS, THE FARMER RESORTS TO SELLING CROPS TO FEED PROCESSORS OUT OF THE AREA, CAUSING THE ORGANIC FEED CONSUMER TO BUY OUT OF THE AREA AS WELL. THIS CREATES SIGNIFICANT ADDED COSTS FOR BOTH BUYER AND SELLER. THIS PROJECT WOULD ADDRESS THE SUPPLY CHAIN ISSUE DIRECTLY. THE ACTIVITIES TO BE PERFORMED WOULD BE TO PURCHASE AND INSTALL VARIOUS MACHINERY AND EQUIPMENT TO BE USED TO EFFICIENTLY AND ACCURATELY CONVERT ORGANIC CROPS INTO PRECISE ANIMAL FEEDS. THIS WOULD ENABLE US TO CREATE A MARKETPLACE FOR ORGANIC ANIMAL FEEDS. THE MARKETPLACE WOULD CREATE DELIVERABLE ORGANIC FEED PRODUCTS THAT WOULD INCLUDE FORMULATED PELLETS, TOTAL MIXED RATIONS, AND PROCESSED COMMODITIES THAT COULD BE USED INDIVIDUALLY OR INCORPORATED INTO THE CUSTOMER S MIXED RATION FOR THEIR FEEDING OPERATION. THE EXPECTED OUTCOMES WOULD BE AN INCREASED PROCESSING CAPACITY IN THE AREA FOR ORGANIC CROP FARMERS AND INCREASED CONSUMPTION OF LOCAL ORGANIC FEEDS. LOCAL ORGANIC PRODUCERS WOULD BENEFIT FROM HAVING THE OPTION OF SELLING THEIR CROPS WITHOUT THE ADDED COST OF MARKETING AND TRANSPORTATION. ORGANIC FEED CONSUMERS WOULD EXPERIENCE THE SAME BENEFIT WITH THE ADDITIONAL BENEFIT OF BEING ABLE TO PURCHASE FEED IN QUANTITIES THAT BETTER ALIGNS WITH THE NEEDS OF THEIR OPERATIONS. INSTEAD OF HAVING TO PURCHASE FULL TRUCK LOADS OR TRAIN CAR LOADS OF A PARTICULAR FEED TO HELP SPREAD THE COST OF FREIGHT OUT, THEY COULD PURCHASE IN AMOUNTS LESS THAN THAT WITHOUT FREIGHT COSTS BEING THE PRIMARY DRIVER IN THEIR DECISIONS. THE FARMER SELLING THE CROPS AND THE CONSUMER PURCHASING THE FEED WILL BOTH BE THE BENEFICIARIES OF BETTER FINANCIAL RETURNS TO THEIR OPERATION FROM THIS PROJECT. WHICH IN TURN, COULD CREATE AN OPPORTUNITY FOR OTHER NON-ORGANIC OPERATIONS TO CONSIDER TRANSITIONING THEIR BUSINESS TO ORGANIC IN THE FUTURE. DARRELL FUNK FARMS, EAGLEVIEW DAIRY, AND STREAMLINE PRECISION WILL ALL PLAY KEY ROLES IN THIS PROJECT. DARRELL FUNK FARMS GROWS OVER 10,000 ACRES OF ORGANIC CROPS ANNUALLY. EAGLEVIEW DAIRY FEEDS OVER 2,100 ORGANIC MILK COWS EVERYDAY. BOTH OF THESE OPERATIONS HAVE COMMITTED TO SUPPORTING THIS PROJECT BY EITHER SELLING COMMODITIES OR PURCHASING FEED FROM THE MARKETPLACE. STREAMLINE PRECISION IS A FULL-SERVICE CONTRACTOR THAT SPECIALIZES IN LARGE-SCALE, COMMERCIAL PROJECTS. THEY HAVE THE EXPERTISE AND EQUIPMENT TO COORDINATE AND DELIVER ON ALL PHASES OF THIS PROJECT. STREAMLINE PRECISION HAS MANUFACTURING AND CONTRACTING ALL UNDER ONE ROOF - MAKING COORDINATED, ACCURATE, CONFIDENTIAL AND CONSISTENT TIMELINES. THROUGH OUR COMBINED EFFORTS AND KNOWLEDGE, THIS PROJECT PROMISES TO BE A RESOUNDING SUCCESS FOR THE RAPIDLY GROWING ORGANIC MARKET.

THE PURPOSE OF THIS PROJECT IS TO PURCHASE AN AIR SCREEN CLEANER AND CROP HANDLING EQUIPMENT TO ENABLE VILICUS FARMS IN MAINTAINING, EXPANDING AND CREATING NEW MARKETS IN MONTANA (AND BEYOND) FOR ORGANIC RYE, GRAINS, LEGUMES, ORGANIC ANIMAL FEED, AND ORGANIC SEED. THIS $101,150 INVESTMENT SIGNIFICANTLY UPGRADES THE FARMS SEED CLEANING CAPACITY (BOTH QUANTITY AND QUALITY) AND INCREASES OPERATIONAL EFFICIENCY BY LOCATING ALL CLEANING EQUIPMENT AT ONE SITE WITH DEDICATED STORAGE AND HANDLING FACILITIES.  THE FARM IS CURRENTLY SELLING IDENTIFY PRESERVED RYE TO TWO CRAFT DISTILLERS IN MONTANA.  THIS PROJECT MAINTAINS THOSE RELATIONSHIPS AND ENABLES MORE DIRECT SALES OF IDENTITY-PRESERVED SINGLE ORIGIN ORGANIC RYE AND GRAINS TO OTHER DISTILLERS AND FARMS WHO WISH TO OFFER A GRAIN AND OR LEGUMES AS PART OF THEIR VEGETABLE COMMUNITY SUPPORTED AGRICULTURE PROGRAMS (CSAS). THIS INCLUDES 70 SHAREHOLDERS IN VILICUS FARMS COMMUNITY SUPPORTED STEWARDSHIP AGRICULTURE PROGRAM.  SCREENINGS FROM CLEANING ACTIVITIES WILL BE SOLD AS ANIMAL FEED, CREATING A NEW PRODUCT FOR THE FARM AND NEW FARM TO FARM RELATIONSHIPS. THE EQUIPMENT INVESTMENT WILL ALSO SUPPORT CLEANING SEED FOR ON-FARM USE AND POTENTIAL SALES TO OTHER FARMERS.  THIS WILL START TO BUILD A MARKET FOR ORGANIC SEED, WHICH DOES NOT CURRENTLY EXIST.   FINALLY, IN COLLABORATION WITH THE MONTANA ORGANIC PRODUCERS COOPERATIVE, THE FARM WILL ASSIST OTHER ORGANIC PRODUCERS, BY CLEANING THEIR CROPS AND TAKE ADVANTAGE OF LARGER OUT OF STATE MARKET OPPORTUNITIES FOR ORGANIC GRAINS.  SALES TO THESE MARKETS HAVE BEEN STYMIED DUE TO LIMITED ORGANIC PROCESSING INFRASTRUCTURE IN MONTANA. VILICUS FARMS IS CURRENTLY HAULING UNCLEANED GRAIN 170 MILES ONE WAY TO BE PROCESSED.  THE SCREENINGS USUALLY CANNOT BE RETAINED AND THERE IS LIMITED FLEXIBILITY FROM THESE PROCESSORS ON SCHEDULE AND QUANTITIES.  ANNUAL INCREASED ORGANIC PRODUCTION AND SALES ESTIMATES ARE:  275,000LBS OF DIRECT SALES ($141,900 GROSS), 101,000LBS OF SCREENINGS FOR ANIMAL FEED ($29,000), 702,000LBS OF SEED FOR ON-FARM USE AND POTENTIAL SALE TO OTHER FARMERS, AND CLEANING FOR OTHERS 1,950,000LBS ($48,750).  THIS INCOME WILL SUPPORT THE TRANSITION OF TWO SEASONAL EMPLOYEES TO FULLTIME, YEAR-ROUND EMPLOYEES.  BENEFICIARIES OF THIS PROJECT ARE IN MONTANA AND FAR BEYOND. CURRENT COLLABORATORS REPRESENT FOUR STATES OUTSIDE OF MONTANA AND CANADA.  THIS PROJECT INCREASES THE CONSUMPTION OF DOMESTIC ORGANIC CROPS, AND IT GROWS CONSUMER AWARENESS ABOUT ORGANIC AGRICULTURE THROUGH DIRECT CONNECTIONS TO ORGANIC FARM COMMUNITIES IN MONTANA AND WASHINGTON. THIS PROJECT IMPACTS 4 DISTILLERIES IN MONTANA, ONE WHICH IS JUST OUTSIDE OF GLACIER NATIONAL PARK AND HAS A TREMENDOUS CUSTOMER BASE.  ANYTIME SPRITZ, IS THE FIRST REGENERATIVE ORGANIC CERTIFIED SPIRITS COMPANY AND IS COMMITTED TO STORY-TELLING ABOUT THEIR SUPPLY CHAIN IN A WAY THAT BENEFITS THE FARM.   40 CENTURY RYE, ANOTHER NEW REGENERATIVE ORGANIC BAKING MIX COMPANY IS INVOLVED IN CREATING A BIODIVERSITY MARKETPLACE ROOTED IN ORGANIC AGRICULTURE, AND MUST BE BASED IN A DIRECT FARM RELATIONSHIP AND IDENTITY PRESERVED PRODUCTS.  GRUFF GRITS PRAIRIE GRASS RANCH, BASED IN MONTANA, WILL EXPAND THEIR PRODUCT LINE TO INCLUDE RYE.   ABRAXAS FARMS WILL USE SCREENINGS FOR THEIR HERITAGE HOG OPERATION.  APRIL JOY FARM WILL TEACH HER CSA MEMBERS AND OTHER CSA FARMS IN WASHINGTON ABOUT ORGANIC GRAINS. SARAH KELLOGG OF POLLY-LABS WILL HELP IDENTIFY ADDITIONAL BUYERS AND PROCESSING INFRASTRUCTURE.  VILICUS FARMS IS WELL KNOWN AND IS COMMITTED TO THE EXPANSION OF ORGANIC AGRICULTURE. AS A FIRST-GENERATION FARM, GROWING A DIVERSE SET OF CROPS AND INTEGRATING LIVESTOCK ACROSS 12,500 ACRES, THEIR FARM OPERATIONS ARE A MODEL FOR WHAT AGRICULTURE NEEDS TO BECOME TO BE MORE CLIMATE RESILIENT.  THIS PROJECT WILL GROW THAT RESILIENCE BY BUILDING A NETWORK OF OVER 15 FARMERS AND SMALL BUSINESSES WHO CARE ABOUT ORGANIC FOOD FOR THEMSELVES, THEIR CONSUMERS AND THEIR ANIMALS USING IDENTITY PRESERVED DIRECT SALES.

DESPITE HAVING A HIGH DENSITY OF SMALL FARMS, SOUTHERN CALIFORNIA FACES A SIGNIFICANT LACK OF CERTIFIED ORGANIC PROCESSING FACILITIES, AN ISSUE THAT NEGATIVELY AFFECTS SMALL AND UNDERSERVED FARMS WHICH RELY ON TIME-CONSUMING, COSTLY HAND LABOR TO PROCESS THEIR ORGANIC COMMODITIES AND CREATE VALUE-ADDED PRODUCTS. TO ADDRESS THIS CHALLENGING ISSUE, THE ECOLOGY CENTER (TEC), A 28-ACRE REGENERATIVE ORGANIC CERTIFIED AND ORGANIC CERTIFIED NON-PROFIT FARM, ON-SITE FARM STAND FOR ORGANIC PRODUCE AND VALUE-ADDED PRODUCTS, AND EDUCATION CENTER, WILL USE GRANT FUNDING TO EXPAND ITS PROCESSING AND DISTRIBUTION CAPACITY FOR VALUE-ADDED PRODUCTS MADE FROM ORGANIC CORN, LEGUMES (BEANS), AND FRUIT. THE GOAL OF THIS PROJECT IS TO PROVIDE A SHARED PROCESSING SERVICE THAT WILL BENEFIT SMALL, LOCAL, ORGANIC FARMS AND FACILITATE THEIR ACCESS TO ORGANIC MARKETS.TEC WILL RENOVATE ITS ON-SITE PROCESSING WAREHOUSE FOR FOOD SAFETY REGULATIONS AND TO ACCOMMODATE NEW PROCESSING EQUIPMENT FOR ORGANIC CORN, LEGUMES, AND FRUIT. TEC WILL ALSO STRENGTHEN PARTNERSHIPS WITH THE SOUTHERN CALIFORNIAN ORGANIC FARM COMMUNITY AND GROW THE SHARED BENEFIT OF INCREASED REGIONAL PROCESSING CAPACITY. NEW PROCESSING EQUIPMENT AND INCREASED PARTNERSHIPS WILL ALLOW FOR SCALED PRODUCTION OF HIGH-DEMAND ORGANIC VALUE-ADDED PRODUCTS INCLUDING JAMS, TORTILLAS, DRIED BEANS, AND SAUCES, AND TEC WILL EXPAND SALES CHANNELS FOR DISTRIBUTION.THIS PROJECT WILL INCREASE ORGANIC VALUE-ADDED PRODUCTION BY 7X IN THE FIRST YEAR OF PRODUCTION, RESULTING IN A TOTAL OF 80,000 LBS OR MORE OF ORGANIC CORN, LEGUMES, AND FRUIT PROCESSED INTO 372,000 OR MORE UNITS OF ORGANIC VALUE-ADDED PRODUCTS BY THE END OF THE GRANT PERIOD. THE PROJECT WILL INCREASE THE CONSUMPTION OF DOMESTICALLY PRODUCED ORGANIC PRODUCTS BY REACHING AT LEAST 40,000 NEW CUSTOMERS AND INFLUENCING UP TO 400,000 NEW CONSUMERS THROUGH THE ADDITION OF 10 OR MORE NEW SALES CHANNELS BY THE END OF THE GRANT PERIOD. THE INVESTMENT IN ORGANIC PROCESSING CAPACITY IN THE REGION WILL FACILITATE MARKET ACCESS FOR 15 OR MORE SOUTHERN CALIFORNIAN ORGANIC PRODUCERS (AT LEAST 10 SMALL, BEGINNER, OR UNDERSERVED FARMS) BY THE END OF THE PROJECT PERIOD.THE PROJECT WILL BENEFIT SOUTHERN CALIFORNIAN ORGANIC PRODUCERS. PROVIDING A SHARED PROCESSING FACILITY FOR LOCAL ORGANIC FARMERS, WHICH WOULD OTHERWISE BE UNAVAILABLE IN THE REGION, WILL REMOVE BARRIERS TO THE ORGANIC MARKET FOR SMALLER LOCAL FARMS BY REDUCING OPERATING COSTS FROM TIME-CONSUMING HAND-PROCESSING AND INCREASING EFFICIENCY AND PROFITABILITY THROUGH NEW EQUIPMENT AND INCREASED DISTRIBUTION.ENGAGEMENT WITH THE PROJECT PARTNERS, SMALL-SCALE ORGANIC FARMS IN SOUTHERN CALIFORNIA, WILL SUPPORT THE DEVELOPMENT OF NEW AND IMPROVED MARKETS FOR DOMESTIC ORGANIC PRODUCTS. BY COLLABORATING WITH MULTIPLE ORGANIC PRODUCERS FOR ORGANIC PROCESSING AND VALUE-ADDED PRODUCTION, IT WILL ALLOW FOR SCALED PRODUCTION AND DISTRIBUTION OF ORGANIC PRODUCTS, AND INCREASE THE CONSUMPTION OF DOMESTICALLY, AND LOCALLY, PRODUCED ORGANIC COMMODITIESINDUCING APPROXIMATELY $2.2 MILLION IN SALES BY THE PROJECTS THIRD YEAR TO BENEFIT AT LEAST 15 LOCAL ORGANIC FARMS.

FARMER GROUND FLOUR BUYS AND PROCESSES A DIVERSITY OF ORGANIC GRAIN CROPS, PAYING A PREMIUM TO LOCAL FARMERS AND PROVIDING A MARKET FOR ORGANIC CROPS NOT OTHERWISE GROWN IN NEW YORK. WE CONTRACT WITH LOCAL FARMERS FOR HARD WHEAT, WHICH IS TRADITIONALLY GROWN IN WESTERN STATES, IN ORDER TO PRODUCE BREAD FLOUR FOR THE NORTHEAST MARKET. BY SHORTENING THE SUPPLY CHAIN AND REDUCING FOOD MILES, THE CARBON FOOTPRINT OF OUR FLOUR IS REDUCED RELATIVE TO THE INDUSTRY STANDARD.THIS PROJECT WILL HELP US INCREASE OUR ANNUAL GRAIN CLEANING AND MILLING CAPACITY, INCREASING THE VOLUME OF GRAIN PURCHASED. BY UPGRADING OUR GRAIN CLEANING AND FLOUR MILLING SYSTEMS SIMULTANEOUSLY, WE WILL HAVE GREATER CAPABILITIES FROM START TO FINISH WITHOUT BOTTLENECKS. A NEW GRAIN CLEANER WILL ENABLE US TO PROCESS CROPS FOR LONG-TERM STORAGE EFFICIENTLY AND WITH LESS WASTE, AND A NEW PAIR OF MILLS WILL INCREASE OUR HOURLY MILLING CAPABILITY. THE OUTCOME IS THAT OUR CAPACITY WILL INCREASE BY 50 . THIS WILL BENEFIT EXISTING REGIONAL ORGANIC FARMERS, AND THOSE HOPING TO TRANSITION TO ORGANIC, WHO WILL HAVE INCREASED MARKET ACCESS TO A PREMIUM PRICE FOR A DIVERSE RANGE OF CROPS.

FERREIRA   SON DAIRY IS LOCATED IN ARCATA, CALIFORNIA, AND IS RUN BY DARIN FERREIRA, A THIRD GENERATION DAIRY FARMER. DARINS GRANDPARENTS MOVED FROM FERNDALE, CALIFORNIA NORTH TO THE ARCATA BOTTOMS TO BEGIN THE DAIRY AFTER THE FLOOD IN 1955, AND DARIN TOOK OVER RUNNING THE FAMILY BUSINESS IN 2018.  THE DAIRY HAS BEEN CERTIFIED ORGANIC SINCE 2007 AND BECAME CERTIFIED GRASS FED IN 2016.  HISTORIC DROUGHT AND INCREASING FEED COSTS IN RECENT YEARS HAVE FORCED LOCAL DAIRIES TO MAKE HARD DECISIONS ABOUT THE FUTURE OF THEIR GENERATIONAL BUSINESSES. IN RESPONSE TO THESE INDUSTRY AND CLIMATE -BASED CHALLENGES, FERREIRA   SON DAIRY HAS EMBARKED ON A FIVE YEAR PLAN TO REMAIN SELF-SUFFICIENT BY EXPANDING AND DIVERSIFYING PRODUCTION, TAKING OVER THEIR OWN DISTRIBUTION THEREBY CUTTING THE COSTS OF MIDDLE DISTRIBUTORS. DURING THE FIRST YEAR, 2021-2022, FERRIERA   SON DAIRY COMPLETED THE FIRST PHASE OF THIS EXPANSION, BUILDING HUMBOLDT COUNTYS FIRST TRULY LOCAL MILK PROCESSING AND BOTTLING PLANT. THE MILK IS PROCESSED RIGHT FROM THE TANK, BOTTLED INTO GLASS BOTTLES, THEN DISTRIBUTED DIRECTLY TO LOCAL STORES,. THE NEXT PHASE OF THE PROJECT IS THE ACQUISITION OF EQUIPMENT TO EXPAND PRODUCTION. THE FUNDS FROM THIS OPPORTUNITY WILL ENABLE THE DAIRY TO PURCHASE EQUIPMENT THAT WILL QUADRUPLE PRODUCTION WITH DIVERSIFIED FATS PERCENTAGES THAT CAN BE USED TO DEVELOP, PRODUCE AND DISTRIBUTE OTHER PRODUCTS THAT WILL GENERATE MORE INCOME FOR THE DAIRY AND INCREASE GROWTH OF THE MARKET FOR ORGANIC PRODUCTS OVERALL IN THE LOCAL ECONOMY. CURRENTLY, FERREIRA   SON DAIRY HAS LIMITED STORAGE CAPACITY, AND USES A MANUAL SINGLE-VALVE BOTTLE FILLER TO PRODUCE ITS MILK PRODUCTS. FUNDS FROM THIS GRANT OPPORTUNITY WILL BE USED TO PURCHASE FOUR ESSENTIAL PIECES OF EQUIPMENT FOR THE NEXT PHASE OF EXPANSION:  A C-STAINLESS TWO-VALVE FILLER, A 600 GALLON DOUBLE WALL TANK, A 700 GALLON PITCHED BOTTOM AGITATED TANK AND A 5 FOOT C-STAINLESS 5-FOOT COP VAT AUTOMATIC EQUIPMENT WASHER AND STERILIZER.  THE 600 GALLON DOUBLE WALL TANK IS NEEDED FOR INCREASED MILK STORAGE. THE TWO VALVE FILLER WILL ALLOW FOR PACKAGING FLUID MILK INTO GLASS BOTTLES OR PLASTIC JUGS. CURRENTLY THE DAIRY USES EXCLUSIVELY GLASS BOTTLES, BUT WITH THE NEW MACHINE, THE DAIRY WILL BE ABLE TO PROVIDE PRODUCTS FOR THE CAL POLY HUMBOLDT UNIVERSITY SYSTEM . THE FILLER CAN ACCOMMODATE A VARIETY OF FLUIDS, INCLUDING REGULAR MILK, FLAVORED MILK, EGG NOG, ETC. THE EQUIPMENT CAN FILL UP TO 10 BOTTLES PER MINUTE, A SUBSTANTIAL INCREASE FROM THE CURRENT SINGLE-VALVE AUTOMATIC FILLER AND THE DESIGN ALLOWS FOR MORE EFFICIENT CHANGES TO BOTTLE SIZES TO ACCOMMODATE ORDERS FROM VARYING MARKETS. THIS EQUIPMENT WILL INCREASE THE CAPACITY OF DAIRY PRODUCTION FROM 300 TO 2000 GALLONS PER WEEK, INCREASING NET SALES FROM $120K PER YEAR TO APPROXIMATELY $480K. THE AUTOMATIC COP VAT UNIT WILL ENABLE THE DAIRY TO KEEP UP WITH THE CAPACITY OF THE NEW FILLER AND MEET STERILIZATION REQUIREMENTS FOR VARIOUS DAIRY PRODUCTS SUCH ICE CREAM.HERE IN HUMBOLDT, THERE IS A STRONG CULTURE OF SUPPORT FOR LOCAL FOOD AND DAIRY PRODUCERS, AND FOR ORGANIC FARMS OF ALL FORMS, BUT ESPECIALLY FOR ORGANIC AND GRASS-FED DAIRY PRODUCTS AND LOCAL PRODUCERS ARE SEEING LOCAL DEMAND FOR MORE VARIETIES OF DAIRY PRODUCTS. IN 2016, HUMBOLDT COUNTY DAIRY FARMS CONTRIBUTED APPROXIMATELY $251M IN REVENUE TO THE STATE. CURRENTLY, THE FERREIRA   SON DAIRY PRODUCES AND DISTRIBUTES WHOLE MILK AND HAS DISTRIBUTION IN ALL LOCAL GROCERY MARKETS, INCLUDING FIELDBROOK MARKET, INDIANOLA MARKET, EUREKA NATURAL FOODS, MURPHYS MARKETS, NORTH COAST CO-OPS, MYRMYRTLE AVENUE, EUREKA) AND DAZEYS (ARCATA). WITH THE PURCHASE OF THE EQUIPMENT, THE DAIRY WILL BE ABLE TO IMMEDIATELY START PRODUCING AND DISTRIBUTING ICE CREAM AND BUTTER, IN ADDITION TO VARYING MILK-FAT PERCENTAGE PRODUCTS TO ALL OF THESE CURRENT DISTRIBUTION MARKETS. OVER THE NEXT FIVE YEARS, FERREIRA   SON DAIRY PLANS TO ALSO INTRODUCE THEIR YOGURT AND CHEESE INTO THE LOCAL ORGANIC MARKET ECONOMY.

OUR PROJECT WILL IMPROVE THE EFFICIENCY, ACCURACY, AND SAFETY OF THE GRAIN HANDLING PROCESS WHILE MEETING THE HIGH-QUALITY STANDARDS DEMANDED BY FOOD-GRADE BUYERS. BY IMPLEMENTING NEW EQUIPMENT AND SYSTEMS, OUR PROJECT WILL STREAMLINE GRAIN FILLING, MEASURING, AND PALLETIZING, THEREBY ENHANCING MARKET ACCESS FOR ORGANIC PRODUCTS AND STRENGTHENING GRANOR FARM S POSITION IN THE ORGANIC GRAIN MARKET.ACTIVITIES TO BE PERFORMED: OUR PROJECT ACTIVITIES INVOLVE THREE PRIMARY OBJECTIVES:1) INCREASE CAPACITY TO FILL, MEASURE, AND PALLETIZE SUPERSACK TOTES OF IDENTITY-PRESERVED ORGANIC GRAINS TO CATER TO VARIOUS END-USERS.2) ELIMINATE EXCESSIVE GRAIN DAMAGE AND LOT CONTAMINATION DURING PACKAGING AND POST-HARVEST HANDLING OF ORGANIC GRAINS.3) INCREASE GRAIN SHIPPING CAPACITY AND MINIMIZE WORKPLACE HAZARDS WHILE FILLING GRAIN SUPERSACKS.DELIVERABLES AND EXPECTED OUTCOMES: THE MAIN DELIVERABLES OF THE PROJECT INCLUDE THE ACQUISITION AND IMPLEMENTATION OF TWO KEY PIECES OF EQUIPMENT: THE UNVERFERTH 3955 DUAL-COMPARTMENT SEED TENDER AND THE BRANDT 1535 LPTD FIELD LOADER CONVEYOR. THEIR ENGAGEMENT IS VITAL TO PROVIDING THE UNVERFERTH 3955 DUAL-COMPARTMENT SEED TENDER AND THE BRANDT 1535 LPTD FIELD LOADER CONVEYOR, RESPECTIVELY. GIANFORTE FARM IS A CERTIFIED ORGANIC GRAIN FARM THAT FARMS APPROXIMATELY 800 ACRES AND CURRENTLY GRINDS FEED FOR LOCAL DAIRY AND LIVESTOCK PRODUCERS IN LIMITED QUANTITIES. THIS GRANT ALLOWS FOR THE INSTALLATION OF A BLOWER SYSTEM AND TWO DEDICATED FEED STORAGE BINS TO THE OPERATION. CURRENTLY, THERE IS NO CAPABILITY TO STORE GROUND FEED, WHICH GREATLY LIMITS THE CAPACITY TO SUPPLY PRODUCERS WITH LOCAL FEED. WHEN A CUSTOMER WANTS A GROUND FEED COMMODITY, THE PRODUCT MUST BE MOVED FROM STORAGE TO THE HAMMER MILL FOR GRINDING, AND THE GRINDING PROCESS TAKE APPROXIMATELY 6 HOURS PER LOAD BECAUSE IT MUST BE GROUND DIRECTLY INTO A WAITING TRUCK. THIS MEANS THE GRINDING PROCESS MUST BE DONE DURING AMENABLE WEATHER AND WATCHED VIRTUALLY CONTINUOUSLY, SINCE THE TRUCK MUST BE MOVED PERIODICALLY TO ENSURE A BALANCED LOAD. OVERALL, THE NATURE OF THE CURRENT SET UP LIMITS THE OPERATION S OUTPUT OF GROUND FEED. WITH THE ADDITION OF THE GROUND FEED STORAGE BINS, GRAIN COULD BE GROUND THROUGH THE HAMMER MILL IN A MORE CONTINUOUS MANNER, WITHOUT BEING AFFECTED BY WEATHER, TIME OF DAY, OR TRUCK AVAILABILITY BECAUSE IT COULD BE BLOWN DIRECTLY INTO A DEDICATED STORAGE BIN. THE STORAGE BINS WOULD BE UTILIZED FOR GROUND CORN, SOYBEANS, OR ROTATIONAL CROPS SUCH AS TRITICALE, BARLEY, WHEAT, OR OATS. THE PROJECT DIRECTLY IMPROVES THE MARKET FOR DOMESTICALLY PRODUCED LIVESTOCK FEED.MANY OPERATIONS IN THE REGIONAL AGRICULTURAL ECOSYSTEM WOULD BE KEY BENEFICIARIES OF THIS PROJECT. THE SYSTEM WOULD ENHANCE THE ABILITY TO MEET THE NEEDS OF CURRENT CUSTOMERS, WHO WILL HAVE MORE FLEXIBILITY WHEN ORDERING FEED (IN TERMS OF AN INCREASE IN AVAILABLE FEED VOLUME, A SHARP DECREASE IN LEAD TIME REQUIRED WHEN ORDERING FEED, AND LESS UNCERTAINTY DUE TO WEATHER CONSTRAINTS). ADDITIONAL BENEFICIARIES INCLUDE OTHER REGIONAL LIVESTOCK PRODUCERS, WHO WOULD HAVE A SOURCE OF ORGANIC FEED THAT WAS GROWN AND PROCESSED WITHIN 100 MILES OF THEIR FACILITY. THIS OFFERS PRODUCERS AN ADDITIONAL PURCHASING OPTION FOR DOMESTICALLY PRODUCED FEED THAT THEY WOULD NOT HAVE OTHERWISE, AND IN MANY CASES OFFERS VALUABLE TRANSPORTATION EFFICIENCY. FINALLY, THIS PROJECT WILL INCREASE THE NEED TO PURCHASE ORGANIC CORN AND SOYBEANS FROM OTHER LOCAL PRODUCERS, CONTRIBUTING TO THE ENHANCEMENT OF THE DOMESTIC ORGANIC ECONOMY. THIS PROJECT WILL BE COMPLETED WITHIN 6 MONTHS OF THE AWARD. KEY PARTNERS INCLUDE REGIONAL DAIRY AND LIVESTOCK OPERATIONS AS THE CURRENT AND FUTURE GROUND FEED CUSTOMERS, AS WELL AS OTHER ORGANIC GROWERS WHO WOULD SUPPLY NECESSARY CORN AND SOYBEANS. BOTH OF THESE PARTNER CATEGORIES ARE IMPORTANT COMPONENTS OF THE ORGANIC SUPPLY CHAIN AND THE COLLABORATIVE WORK WITH THEM ENHANCES THE DOMESTIC ORGANIC FOOD SUPPLY. THE OTHER KEY PARTNER INVOLVED WILL BE A.N. MARTIN GRAIN SYSTEMS, WHO WILL INSTALL THE NECESSARY EQUIPMENT.

IN 2022, U.S. FARMERS PRODUCED MORE THAN 2.35 BILLION TONS OF GRAIN FEED TO SERVE DOMESTIC AND INTERNATIONAL LIVESTOCK PRODUCERS (USDA ECONOMIC RESEARCH SERVICE). STILL, LESS THAN 1% OF THE GRAIN FEED PRODUCED IN THE UNITED STATES IS ORGANIC, DESPITE STRONG AND CONSISTENT GROWTH IN U.S. DEMAND FOR ORGANIC FOOD. WITH MORE THAN 82 PERCENT OF U.S. HOUSEHOLDS BUYING ORGANIC PRODUCTS REGULARLY (ORGANIC TRADE ASSOCIATION), THE ORGANIC CENTER NOTES THAT DRIVEN BY GROWTH IN DEMAND FOR U.S. ORGANIC LIVESTOCK FEED THE U.S. HAS BECOME A SUBSTANTIAL NET IMPORTER OF ORGANIC PRODUCTS. IN FACT, U.S. IMPORTS OF GRAIN FEED HAVE STEADILY INCREASED OVER THE PAST DECADE, GROWING FROM 40 PERCENT IN THE 2011 12 CROP YEAR TO 60 PERCENT IN THE 2021 2022 CROP YEAR. THIS IS PRIMARILY DUE TO THE MAJOR BARRIERS THAT EXIST TO PRODUCING, PROCESSING, AND MARKETING ORGANIC GRAIN FEED, NAMELY HIGHER COSTS OF PRODUCTION AND LACK OF PROCESSING AND MARKETING INFRASTRUCTURE. TO MEET CURRENT U.S. CONSUMER DEMAND AND EXPAND OPPORTUNITIES TO BUILD THE U.S. ORGANIC GRAIN FEED MARKET (PROJECT PURPOSE), GRANGE COOPERATIVE WILL PERFORM THE FOLLOWING ACTIVITIES: 1) EXPAND ITS PROCESSING CAPACITY TO CREATE MORE AND BETTER MARKETS FOR ORGANIC PRODUCERS  AND 2) EXECUTE MARKETING AND PROMOTIONAL ACTIVITIES THAT WILL HELP TO BUILD COMMERCIAL MARKETS FOR U.S. ORGANIC GRAIN FEED PRODUCTS. THIS PROJECTS GOALS (DELIVERABLES AND EXPECTED OUTCOMES) INCLUDE ACHIEVING 2,000 ADDITIONAL TONS OF ORGANIC GRAIN FEED PROCESSED AND A $1,655,000 INCREASE IN DOMESTIC ORGANIC GRAIN FEED SALES BY THE END OF THE PROJECT PERIOD. KEY PARTNERS INCLUDE 100 PACIFIC NORTHWEST ORGANIC LIVESTOCK PRODUCERS (INTENDED BENEFICIARIES), FEED MARKETING LLC, AMERICAN FEED INDUSTRY ASSOCIATION, CONCENTRATES, INC, AND OREGON GRAIN AND FEED ASSOCIATION.

OUR GOAL IS TO CREATE A MARKET FOR WOOL IN THE HORTICULTURAL INDUSTRY TO REPLACE PRODUCTS CURRENTLY USED WITH MORE SUSTAINABLE, CERTIFIABLE ORGANIC PRODUCTS THAT WILL BENEFIT BOTH SHEEP AND CROP FARMERS. THE ONLY REGIONAL AGGREGATOR OF WOOL FROM SHEARING HAS STOPPED BUYING WOOL. SHEEP FARMING IN OHIO IS INCREASING, AND WITH IT, WOOL PRODUCTION. COARSE AND LOW-GRADE WOOL CAN SUBSTITUTE SOIL AMENDMENTS AND WEED SUPPRESSION MATERIALS USED IN HORTICULTURE. WOOL STORES UP TO 33 OF ITS WEIGHT IN WATER AND SLOWLY RELEASES WATER ONCE THE SURROUNDING ENVIRONMENT DROPS BELOW 65 RELATIVE HUMIDITY, IS FULLY DEGRADABLE, CONTAINS NITROGEN, CALCIUM, MAGNESIUM, IRON, SULFUR, AND OTHER MICRO NUTRIENTS. FELTED WOOL MATS CAN REPLACE PLASTIC WEED BARRIERS. THEY CAN REGULATE SOIL TEMPERATURES, PREVENT MOISTURE LOSS, ADD FERTILIZER, ACT AS A PEST BARRIER TO SLUGS AND SNAILS, AND PROVIDE EXCELLENT WEED PREVENTION. SHREDDED WOOL CAN BE MIXED WITH SEED TO BE A DELIVERY METHOD FOR HABITAT RESTORATION, LANDSCAPING AND CROP ESTABLISHMENT.SOIL AND POTTING MIXES ARE CURRENTLY AMENDED WITH PEAT, VERMICULITE, AND PERLITE TO INCREASE THE WATER-HOLDING CAPACITY AND PROVIDE AERATION. ADVERSE ECOLOGICAL TO THESE SOIL AMENDMENTS INCLUDE THE DEPLETION OF PEAT BOGS AND THE HIGH CARBON FOOTPRINT OF VERMICULITE AND PERLITE FROM TRANSPORTATION AND OVERSEAS MINING OPERATIONS. WOOL PELLETS CAN PROVIDE AERATION, HOLD MOISTURE AND ARE NATURALLY HIGH IN NITROGEN MAKING THEM THE PERFECT SLOW-RELEASE, ALL-NATURAL FERTILIZER.

LITTLE SESAME WILL EXPAND THE DOMESTIC CERTIFIED ORGANIC CHICKPEA MARKET BY INCREASING AGGREGATION, PROCESSING, AND DISTRIBUTION OF ITS CONSUMER-PACKAGED LINE OF HUMMUS WHILE SIMULTANEOUSLY GROWING CONSUMER DEMAND THROUGH ENHANCED SALES AND MARKETING CAPACITY. OVER THE PAST SEVERAL YEARS, DROUGHTS, FLOODING, AND WAR IN TOP CHICKPEA-PRODUCING COUNTRIES HAS LED TO AN INCREASED MARKET DEMAND FOR DOMESTICALLY-GROWN CHICKPEAS. THAT PAIRED WITH A GROWING INTEREST IN PLANT-BASED FOODS THAT RELY ON CHICKPEAS AND OTHER LEGUMES CREATES A UNIQUE OPPORTUNITY FOR ORGANIC CHICKPEA PRODUCERS IN THE UNITED STATES. THE PURPOSE OF THIS AWARD IS TO FUND THE STATE’S WORK IN SUPPORT OF THE PESTICIDE DATA PROGRAM (PDP).  THE STATE WILL COLLECT FOOD SAMPLES IN THEIR STATE AND SHIP THE SAMPLES TO THE ASSIGNED LABORATORIES PER THE ESTABLISHED SCHEDULE.  THE FOODS, WHICH FOCUS ON THOSE MOST FREQUENTLY CONSUMED BY INFANTS AND CHILDREN, ARE SPECIFIED IN THE CURRENT PDP PROJECT PLAN THAT IS POSTED ON THE PDP WEBSITE.  THE STATE LABORATORY WILL PERFORM CHEMICAL ANALYSES ON THE ASSIGNED SAMPLES FOR PESTICIDE RESIDUES, INCLUDING PARENT COMPOUNDS AND METABOLITES.  THE RESULTS OF THE RESIDUE ANALYSIS WILL BE REVIEWED BY THE STATE QUALITY ASSURANCE OFFICER AND SENT TO PDP AS AN ELECTRONIC DATASET.  ALL WORK WILL BE CONDUCTED ACCORDING TO STANDARD OPERATING PROCEDURES THAT ARE AVAILABLE ON THE PDP WEBSITE. THE DELIVERABLE OF THE SAMPLING OPERATION IS TO PROVIDE THE REQUESTED SAMPLES TO THE LABORATORIES, AND THE DELIVERABLE OF THE LABORATORY IS TO PROVIDE THE PESTICIDE RESIDUE DATA TO PDP.  THE INTENDED BENEFICIARIES INCLUDE THE ENVIRONMENTAL PROTECTION AGENCY, WHO USES THE DATA TO PREPARE DIETARY RISK ASSESSMENTS FOR PESTICIDES; THE FOOD AND DRUG ADMINISTRATION WHO USES THE ROUTINE MONITORING DATA FROM PDP TO INFORM THEIR REGULATORY ENFORCEMENT OF ESTABLISHED LIMITS OF PESTICIDE RESIDUES IN FOOD; THE USDA FOREIGN AGRICULTURAL SERVICE WHO MAY USE THE DATA IN TRADE NEGOTIATIONS; AND AMERICAN CONSUMERS WHO USE THE DATA TO HELP ENSURE THEIR CONFIDENCE IN THE FOOD THEY PURCHASE FOR THEIR FAMILIES.

THIS PROJECT, ENTITLED DIVERSIFYING ORGANIC SUPPLY CHAINS FOR SMALL PRODUCERS IN THE RIO GRANDE VALLEY, WILL INCREASE CONSUMPTION OF LOCALLY PRODUCED ORGANIC ORANGE JUICE IN THE RIO GRANDE VALLEY AND INCREASE THE PROFITABILITY AND LONG-TERM VIABILITY OF TRIPLE J ORGANICS THROUGH SPECIAL PURPOSE EQUIPMENT PURCHASES OF COMMERCIAL JUICING EQUIPMENT AND A REFRIGERATED DELIVERY TRAILER. THE NEW EQUIPMENT WILL ENABLE TRIPLE J TO PROCESS 32,000 LBS. OF WASTE OR SECONDS ORANGES INTO FRESH JUICE AND DELIVER IT SAFELY TO NEW AND EXISTING CUSTOMERS IN THE VALLEY OVER TWO YEARS. IN DOING SO, TRIPLE J WILL INCREASE REVENUE ON ORANGES BY 36 . ACTIVITIES INCLUDE COORDINATING PURCHASE OF THE EQUIPMENT, USING AND EVALUATING THE EQUIPMENT FOR TARGETED OUTCOMES, AND COMPLETING USDA REPORTING. THE PROJECT IS SUPPORTED BY THE TEXAS CENTER FOR LOCAL FOOD, SUSTAINABLE FOOD CENTER, AND UNIVERSITY OF TEXAS RIO GRANDE VALLEY CENTER FOR SARA, WHO ARE COMMITTED TO PROVIDING TRIPLE J WITH TECHNICAL ASSISTANCE AROUND MARKET DEVELOPMENT AND REPORTING. THE PROJECT WILL TARGET SCHOOL DISTRICTS AS POTENTIAL CUSTOMERS, AS WELL AS SUPERMARKETS, RESTAURANTS, HEALTH FOOD STORES, DAYCARE FACILITIES, AND ELDERCARE FACILITIES AS NEEDED. BENEFICIARIES INCLUDE TRIPLE J ORGANICS, LOCAL SCHOOLS AND BUSINESSES WHO PURCHASE THE NEW PRODUCT, AS WELL AS OTHER ORGANIC CITRUS GROWERS IN THE VALLEY WHO MAY BE ABLE TO COOPERATE AND AGGREGATE TO PRODUCE A HIGHER MARGIN VALUE-ADDED PRODUCT.

VALLEY MALT, DBA GROUND UP, IS A WOMEN-OWNED FLOUR MILL IN HOLYOKE, MA PROPOSING OMDG FUNDING FOR A NORTHEAST ORGANIC ROLLER MILL (NORM) PROJECT DEDICATED TO NORTHEAST ORGANIC GRAINS. THE PURPOSE OF THIS PROJECT IS TO CONTINUE TO FOSTER, COORDINATE, AND EXPAND A REGIONAL DEMAND AND STABLE MARKET FOR ORGANIC CEREAL GRAINS IN THE NORTHEAST. THE GOAL IS FOR GROUND UP TO PURCHASE AN ADDITIONAL 2,600 ACRES OF NORTHEAST ORGANIC GRAINS ANNUALLY BY 2026. THIS PROJECT WILL BEGIN TO MEET A HISTORICALLY UNMET NEED FOR DOMESTIC ORGANIC CEREAL GRAINS AND ADDRESS A PINCH POINT IN OUR FOOD SYSTEM. ESTIMATED SALES OF ORGANIC BREAD AND GRAIN PRODUCTS ARE INCREASING BY 12% ANNUALLY, WELL ABOVE OTHER SECTORS HOWEVER DOMESTIC PRODUCTION OF ORGANIC GRAINS ACCOUNT FOR ONLY 2.6% OF ORGANIC CROP PRODUCTION IN THE US. THIS PROJECT WILL ADDRESS THIS MISMATCH SPECIFICALLY FOR THE NORTHEAST AND AIM TO SUPPORT A REGIONAL GRAINSHED (GRAIN SUPPLY CHAIN). MULTI-STATE COLLABORATIONS BETWEEN THE NORTHEASTS PUBLIC AND PRIVATE SECTORS IN THE LAST 15 YEARS HAVE SUPPORTED THE DEVELOPMENT OF CEREAL GRAIN CULTIVARS ADAPTED TO THE NORTHEAST THAT ARE FAVORED BY BAKERS AND FARMERS ALIKE. REGIONAL RESOURCES FROM UNIVERSITY EXTENSION, AGRONOMISTS, AND PEER-TO-PEER NETWORKS ACROSS THE REGION WILL SUPPORT GROWERS IN PROVIDING 2,600 ACRES ANNUALLY OF ORGANIC GRAINS BY THE END OF THIS PROJECT.INTENDED BENEFICIARIES OF THE PROJECT WILL INCLUDE STAKEHOLDERS FROM THE ENTIRE NORTHEAST GRAIN VALUE CHAIN: SMALL AND MEDIUM SIZED ORGANIC AND TRANSITIONAL GROWERS, DISTRIBUTORS OF ORGANIC FOODS, COMMERCIAL BAKERIES AND INSTITUTIONAL BUYERS, MICRO-BAKERIES, AND SPECIALTY FOOD PRODUCERS FROM UNDERSERVED POPULATIONS, AND APPROXIMATELY 300,000 CONSUMERS OF ORGANIC FOOD IN THE NORTHEAST.

KEY PARTNERS INCLUDE LIGHT OF DAY ORGANICS AND GREAT LAKES GARLIC FARM, BOTH OF WHOM INTEND TO CONTRACT WITH WEINRICH FARM LLC TO PRODUCE ORGANIC ANIMAL FEED ON THEIR PROPERTIES.
